verdict.summary: Building against a Ramp sandbox is quick and self-serve, but an OAuth app that other Ramp businesses can authorize needs Ramp to approve your production access application, which is framed as a partnership with security disclosures (SOC 2, ISO 27001 or a third-party pen test). Only Admin or Business Owner users at each customer can authorize the app.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Ramp's support article says a requested sandbox is ready in about one minute. Creating an app with the Authorization Code grant and scopes in Company → Developer is a few console clicks.

timeToProd.assumes: A multi-tenant agent that other Ramp businesses connect via Authorization Code; an internal tool for your own Ramp business can use Client Credentials the same day with no review.
timeToProd.waitingOn: Ramp's review of your production access application (integration flows plus security disclosures), then an optional beta phase and separate public listing review.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Ramp says approval is required before production access but publishes no timeline. The range is our estimate for a partner review that includes security documentation.

verdict.cost: No fees or revenue share per Ramp's partner guide. Security attestations (SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, or a third-party pen test) are expected, which cost money if you don't already have them.

prerequisites.item: A Ramp sandbox (requested through Ramp's sandbox access form) or a Ramp business where you are an Admin
prerequisites.why: Developer apps are created inside a Ramp account under Company → Developer, and admin access is required.

prerequisites.item: HTTPS redirect URI that exactly matches one configured on the app
prerequisites.why: The Authorization Code flow requires HTTPS redirect URIs and an exact match.
Each environment requires its own app configuration; tokens only work in the environment that issued them.

prerequisites.item: Security package: SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, PCI or a recent third-party pen test report, a public security policy URL and a monitored security contact
prerequisites.why: Partners must complete security disclosures. Early-stage companies may substitute a recent pen test, subject to Ramp's review.

prerequisites.item: Public support email and public setup documentation
prerequisites.why: Ramp routes customer questions to you and expects hosted docs and an internal support guide for Ramp teams.

scopeTiers.impact: With Client Credentials, your own Ramp business can read its data immediately. Enough for an internal agent; not for connecting other companies.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The quickstart uses Client Credentials with transactions:read on your own account.

scopeTiers.impact: Needs approved production access before customers outside your own business can authorize the app. Scopes must be pre-configured on the app or Ramp returns invalid_scope.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Review is tied to production access for multi-business apps, not to specific scopes. Timeline is an estimate.

scopeTiers.impact: Ramp says cards:read_vault requires additional security review, and Vault API docs say production access review is needed before retrieving full PANs and CVVs.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: Time is our estimate; no published SLA.

scopeTiers.impact: Creating financing applications needs a client permitted to access businesses other than its own; restricted clients cannot use the create endpoint.

steps.title: Request a sandbox
steps.detail: Submit Ramp's sandbox access form. You get an access email for a pre-populated demo business at demo.ramp.com.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: Support article says the sandbox should be ready in about one minute.

steps.title: Pick scopes and draft the integration design
steps.detail: Map each endpoint the agent calls to its required scope (start read-only, e.g. transactions:read business:read), and plan sync: synced_after only catches accounting-sync events, so use webhooks or periodic re-pulls for other changes.

steps.title: Create the sandbox developer app
steps.detail: In the sandbox go to Settings → Company → Developer → Create New App, accept terms, add the Authorization Code and Refresh Token grant types, configure allowed scopes and HTTPS redirect URIs, and copy the client ID and secret.

steps.title: Implement the OAuth flow
steps.detail: Redirect to https://demo.ramp.com/v1/authorize (prod: https://app.ramp.com/v1/authorize) with response_type=code, client_id, redirect_uri, scope and a random state. Exchange the code at {api}/developer/v1/token using HTTP Basic auth; API hosts are demo-api.ramp.com and api.ramp.com.

steps.title: Test with sandbox demo actions
steps.detail: Use the ⌘J demo actions panel to create transactions, pay bills and mark reimbursements paid, then verify your agent reads them.

steps.title: Prepare the security and support package
steps.detail: Draft data-processing, storage, retention and employee-access descriptions, the public setup docs, and an internal support guide for Ramp teams.

steps.title: Attach certifications and apply for production access
steps.detail: Provide full SOC 2 / ISO 27001 / pen test reports (not summary letters), security policy URL and security contact, and submit the production access application.

steps.title: Wait for Ramp's review
steps.detail: Ramp reviews your integration flows and gives feedback; approval is required before production access.

steps.title: Create the production app and run beta
steps.detail: Recreate the app in production (separate credentials), point to app.ramp.com/api.ramp.com, and onboard beta customers through OAuth with an Admin or Business Owner at each.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: Beta testing is Phase 3 of Ramp's partner checklist; duration is our estimate.

steps.title: Optionally apply for a public listing
steps.detail: Supply logo, descriptions, screenshots and video for the ramp.com/integrations page.

agentCanDo: Map endpoints to the minimum scopes
Generate the authorize URL and token exchange code
Build pagination, webhook and 429 backoff handling
Draft security disclosures and data-retention text
Write public setup docs and the Ramp support guide
humanMustDo: Request the sandbox and create apps in the console
Obtain SOC 2, ISO 27001 or pen test reports
Recruit beta customers whose Admin authorizes the app

blockers.symptom: "Business not authorized to use this application" on the consent screen
blockers.cause: The person authorizing lacks Developer API authorization permission, typically limited to Admin and Business Owner roles.
blockers.fix: Have an Admin or Business Owner at the customer complete the flow; they can check roles in Settings → Team.

blockers.symptom: invalid_scope from the authorize or token endpoint
blockers.cause: A requested scope isn't configured on the app.
blockers.fix: Add the scope under Configure allowed scopes, then re-authorize; existing tokens can't gain scopes.

blockers.cause: The Refresh Token grant type isn't enabled on the app.
blockers.fix: Add the Refresh Token grant type in app settings.

blockers.symptom: Tokens or credentials rejected after moving to production
blockers.cause: Sandbox and production are isolated; apps, credentials and tokens don't carry over, and API hosts differ from app hosts.
blockers.fix: Create a separate production app and call api.ramp.com, not app.ramp.com.

blockers.symptom: DEVELOPER_7100 errors on reimbursements or spend request endpoints
blockers.cause: Token was issued without the needed scope (reported for a third-party shared OAuth client missing reimbursements:read).
blockers.fix: Request every scope each endpoint needs and re-authorize.

evidence.label: unverified
evidence.note: Pipedream community thread, not Ramp docs.

blockers.symptom: Custom MCP client's OAuth flow fails against Ramp MCP
blockers.cause: Custom MCP clients and third-party gateways must have their exact redirect URI allowlisted by Ramp.
blockers.fix: Submit Ramp's redirect URI allowlist request form, or use the REST API with your own approved app.

nuances.text: Authorization Code access tokens default to 1 hour (can vary per app; use expires_in). Refreshing returns a new access token but not a new refresh token, so keep the original and track refresh_token_expires_in if present.
Client Credentials tokens last about 10 days, return no refresh token, and act with no user context, suitable only for your own business.
Rate limit is 200 requests per 10-second rolling window per source IP; requests over 60 seconds return 504. Higher limits via support ticket.
Authorization codes expire after 10 minutes, and state is required for new integrations.

Ramp also offers an official Ramp MCP server and CLI that act with the signed-in user's permissions; off-the-shelf clients like Claude and ChatGPT work without allowlisting, which may be faster than building your own OAuth app for some agent use cases.
Ramp's docs pages render via JavaScript; the machine-readable text export at docs.ramp.com/llms-guides.txt is the reliable source for agents.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: Docs HTML returned a JS shell pointing to /llms*.txt; llms-guides.txt returned the full guide text on 2026-10-20.
